output.summary: A perennial chilli shrub originating in ancient Peru and across the Andean region of South America, it has white or cream flowers and usually downward-hanging pods with citrus or fruity flavours. Heat varies widely among cultivars. Ají amarillo is used fresh in Peru and dried and ground in Bolivia.
output.edibilityNote: Ají amarillo is used as a condiment, mostly fresh in Peru and dried and ground in Bolivia.
